name: SSHI_FullBridge
rationale: The reference FBR fails mainly due to inefficient energy extraction from the piezo capacitance and poor voltage regulation. I am implementing a Synchronized Switch Harvesting on Inductor (SSHI) topology. By using a switch and an inductor to invert the voltage across the piezo capacitance at its peaks, we significantly increase the energy harvested per cycle. This should improve the average output voltage for heavy (S2) and weak (S4) excitations and speed up the startup time (tup). A Zener diode (DZ33) is added to the output to clamp the voltage at 3.3 V, ensuring vout_max <= 3.6 V even under strong excitation (S3).

name: SECE_Symmetric
rationale: As an alternative to SSHI, I am proposing a Synchronous Electric Charge Extraction (SECE) circuit. SECE is often more efficient because it decouples the piezo's internal capacitance from the load, transferring the accumulated charge to the storage capacitor in a concentrated burst at the voltage extrema. This topology uses two extraction paths (one for each half-cycle) to maximize power. Like the SSHI design, it includes a Zener clamp to prevent overvoltage and a storage capacitor to minimize ripple.

name: SyncBoost_Rectifier
rationale: The previous SSHI_FullBridge failed on startup, ripple, and settling. The high ripple and slow settling were caused by the large storage capacitor needed to buffer the massive energy bursts from the SSHI flip, while the slow startup was due to the diode drops of the full-bridge. This new topology replaces the full-bridge with a synchronous-switch boost rectifier. By using switches (S1, S2) to charge an inductor (L1) during each half-cycle and a single diode (D1) to deliver that energy to the output, we eliminate the voltage drop and provide a more controlled boost. This should allow for a smaller storage capacitor (improving startup and settling) while the inductor's natural smoothing effect helps reduce ripple.

name: SECE_Inductor_Out
rationale: The previous SSHI_FullBridge achieved excellent average voltage and startup time, but failed the ripple requirement. To reduce ripple without significantly increasing the output capacitor (which would slow down the startup time tup), I am moving the inductor and switch from the input (parallel to the piezo) to the output (between the rectifier and the storage capacitor). This is the SECE (Synchronized Electric Charge Extraction) topology. In this configuration, the inductor L1 acts as a current buffer, delivering charge to Cout in more controlled pulses, which should reduce peak-to-peak ripple while maintaining a fast startup and high efficiency.

name: SSHI_LC_Filter
rationale: The SSHI_FullBridge design successfully achieved the target average voltage and startup time, but failed the ripple requirement. The high ripple is a consequence of the energy being delivered in sharp pulses, and increasing the storage capacitor (Cout) to reduce ripple would increase the startup time (tup) beyond the 0.15s limit, especially under weak excitation (S4). To break this trade-off, I am introducing a second inductor (L2) to form a low-pass LC filter between the rectifier and the output capacitor. This inductor smooths the current delivery, reducing the peak-to-peak ripple without significantly increasing the time required to reach 1.8V, as the peak charging current remains high enough during cold start.

name: SSHI_PiFilter
rationale: The SSHI_LC_Filter design is nearly successful, but fails on the ripple requirement (vpp <= 0.02V). To further suppress the charging pulses from the rectifier and reduce output ripple, I am replacing the single-stage LC filter with a pi-filter (C-L-C). Adding a pre-filter capacitor (C2) at the rectifier output node (n_rect) will absorb the bulk of the current spikes, while the existing inductor (L2) and storage capacitor (C1) will further smooth the voltage at the 'out' node. This topology should significantly lower the ripple while maintaining the power extraction benefits of the SSHI stage.

name: SSHI_DoubleL_Filter
rationale: The SSHI_PiFilter was very close to passing, but failed slightly on ripple and startup. The Pi filter (C-L-C) provided good ripple suppression but slowed down the cold start. A Double-L filter (L-C-L-C) offers even more aggressive ripple attenuation (second-order filtering at the output) while potentially allowing for a smaller first capacitor (C2), which can speed up the initial charging process compared to a Pi filter. By using two inductors (L2, L3) and two capacitors (C2, C1), we create a low-pass structure that should push the ripple below 20 mV while keeping the total capacitance manageable for startup within 0.15 s.

name: SSHI_SeriesL_Filter
rationale: The SSHI_LC_Filter was very close to passing but failed on ripple (48-74mV), needing <20mV. To reduce ripple without increasing output capacitance (which slows startup 'tup' and settling 'dv'), I am increasing the total filter inductance by placing two inductors L2 and L3 in series. This increases the total inductance to potentially 20mH, reducing the current ripple. By using a single output capacitor C1 instead of an intermediate one (as in the DoubleL filter), I keep the total capacitance low enough to meet the startup and settling time requirements.
